one_liner: Header-only B-tree replacement for std::map/set/multimap/multiset with C++17 try_emplace API and lower per-element memory.
what_it_does: A template library providing btree::map, btree::set, btree::multimap and btree::multiset as near drop-in replacements for the STL ordered associative containers, built on a B-tree instead of a red-black tree. The API mirrors modern std::map/set: insert, emplace, try_emplace, operator[], find, count, erase, plus a C++20-gated contains() (added per issue #3). It is not a full drop-in: modifying the container invalidates all outstanding iterators, not just erased ones, which is the one documented behavioral break from std::map/std::set semantics.
how_it_is_fast: Each node packs many keys/values into a fixed target size (256 bytes by default, tunable via the TargetNodeSize template parameter) instead of one value per red-black-tree node with three pointers plus color bit, so a lookup does several in-node comparisons per cache line touched rather than one pointer-chasing hop per comparison. The header's own comment attributes the win to better cache locality from this packing, not to a different asymptotic complexity — both are O(log n); a btree::set<int32_t> reportedly uses ~4.9 bytes/element total vs ~20 bytes for the red-black-tree set.
when_to_use: Large in-memory ordered containers of small fixed-size keys (int32/int64) where memory footprint and cache-miss-bound lookup/insert/delete dominate
Workloads with heavy forward iteration, where the header's own numbers show the largest gains (e.g. +83.54% on BM_set_int32_fwditer, +80%+ on int64/map variants)
Call sites that don't retain iterators across mutation (short-lived iterators, no insert/erase while iterating elsewhere)
Willing to vendor a small, unmaintained 3-file header rather than depend on absl::btree or another maintained B-tree
Need per-instantiation control of node size for your specific key/value size
when_not_to_use: String or other expensive-to-move keys/values: gains shrink to single digits (+6.38% string set lookup, +1.16% string set insert) and fifo-pattern workloads regress (-61.01% set_string_fifo, -49.75% map_string_fifo) because rebalancing moves values between nodes
Code that holds iterators across mutation — std::map's stable-iterator guarantee does not hold here; any insert/erase can invalidate unrelated iterators

Need an actively maintained dependency: last commit 2021-01-08, one open unresolved bug (#2: assertion failure / later segfault reachable via operator[] -> try_emplace on a non-trivial value type) with zero maintainer response since it was filed in 2020
Need heterogeneous/transparent lookup (is_transparent-style comparators) — requested in still-open issue #10, not implemented
Need documented thread-safety guarantees — none are given anywhere in the headers; treat it as unsynchronized, same as std::map

integration.dependencies: none beyond the C++ standard library (<algorithm>, <functional>, <memory>, <iterator>, etc.)
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 minimum (variadic templates, forward_as_tuple, piecewise_construct used throughout); README targets C++17-style semantics (try_emplace); contains() only compiles under C++20 (#if __cplusplus > 201703L)
integration.platforms: any — portable C++ template code; no SIMD intrinsics or platform-specific code in btree.h/map.h/set.h
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: same container names and STL-style method surface (insert/emplace/try_emplace/find/erase/operator[]) as std::map/set/multimap/multiset, but modifying the container invalidates ALL outstanding iterators rather than only erased ones, so code relying on std::map's iterator-stability guarantee cannot be ported unmodified

gotchas: Any insert/erase/rebalance invalidates every outstanding iterator on the container, not just ones pointing at removed elements — a real semantic break from std::map/std::set
The header's own CAVEATS comment still points to a 'safe_btree' iterator-safe wrapper as a workaround, but no safe_btree.h ships in this repo — only btree.h, map.h and set.h exist

Open issue #2 (filed 2020-09-24, still unresolved): assertion failure / later segfault in btree_node::construct_value, reached via operator[] -> try_emplace on a non-trivial value type; no maintainer response
Values are moved within and between nodes on every rebalance, so an expensive-to-move value_type can make this slower than std::map despite the smaller footprint
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick cpp-btree over frozenca/BTree or fast-containers when you want a minimal, dependency-free, three-header vendor-in rather than a SIMD-tuned or hugepage-backed B-tree; its own numbers are far more modest (roughly 1.1-1.85x on integer-key ops, near-parity or a regression on strings) than frozenca/BTree's ~4.7-5.2x or fast-containers' ~2.1-4.8x, so prefer those when benchmark rigor and larger margins matter more than a small self-contained header.
verified_claims_summary: The header comment (btree/btree.h, lines ~51-101) reproduces Google's original 2010 btree_bench table comparing the STL red-black-tree set/map against btree::set/map (node size 256) for int32, int64 and string keys/values, run on 'pmattis-warp.nyc (4 X 2200 MHz CPUs)': integer-key ops improve roughly 40-84% (e.g. set_int32_lookup 1160ns to 414ns, set_int32_fwditer 158ns to 26ns), string-key ops improve much less (set_string_lookup 1709ns to 1600ns, +6.38%) and two fifo benchmarks regress (set_string_fifo -61.01%, map_string_fifo -49.75%). No compiler, flags, or exact CPU model are given, and this repo ships no benchmark harness to reproduce the numbers.
status_note: Abandoned since the last real commit on 2021-01-08, with one open, unanswered bug report from 2020; Apache-2.0-licensed, header-only, and small enough (3 header files) to vendor as-is despite the lack of maintenance.
